   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right

From G.W.Hill. WILLENHALL



Dear Ron & Brian.

Many thanks for OUTLET - it's
magic! It's a WINNER! It's what
I have been looking for!

Sorry I did't twig before, I was
getting a little worried that I
would not find or be able to get
any serious programs for the +3.
There was a time when a lot of
programmers were complaining
about the Spectrum not having a
disk drive. Now that it has,they
do not want to know! Where are
they all?

I started off with the ZX81 then
a Spectrum+ and now the ultimate
Spectrum, the +3. You can add
another disk drive to it. I
fully intend to add one to it
this summer. You can add a full-
size printer, I have one, "YES"
I am sticking to my Spectrum +3!
"LETS HEAR IT FOR THE SPECTRUM
+33333333333!!!!!!!!!"

I would like to see you attract
more people to write more
utilities and back up your
writers and give them a prize
"YES" put your money where your
mouth is!!. "YES" `100.00 " -
how's that?"...

1. FOR THE BEST BUSINESS UTILITY
FOR 1990

2. FOR THE BEST HOUSE UTILITY

3. FOR THE BEST SPECTRUM +3
DEDICATED PROGRAM

How about a top ten like the one
in the all the mags we buy but
for utilities writers.

Sorry for carrying on - better
shuta my face.

        Yours faithfully,

          George Hill.

P.S.Please,is it too much to ask
for you to keep +3 disk progs to
the 3". I can't see any sense in
mixing them up.

To George Hill from Brian

The "sense" is that there would
be more work involved in having
each version of OUTLET specific
only to that machine. If, for
example, I remove from the +3
version a program that only
works on a Disciple, I have to
get another program to fill the
space (otherwise what's the
point?).It must be a +3-specific
program because any general
program will eventually appear
in the other versions anyway. It
must be the right size - not too
large and not too small. I might
not have such a program. If I
have, I must then assess it,edit
it, test it, insert it, link it,
re-test it and so on.

It may look like readers send in
programs and I just throw them
on the disc. In reality, MOST
programs take several hours to
prepare and test and MANY have
taken TWO TO THREE DAYS WORK!

I think we have to accept that
in a magazine there will be many
different items - some of great
interest - others we skip over.
All I can do is cram in as much
as possible so everybody finds
sufficient to make it worth the
cost.

We already pay for programs sent
to OUTLET, typically `5 to `25
upwards but may consider an
extra annual cash prize scheme.
What do others think?
                        - Brian

From  Simon Greenfield, LINCOLN

I now have the new ROM and to be
quite honest for twelve quid I
am rather disappointed with it.
Everything you have pointed out
is true and I even notice a bug
which was present with the old
ROM is still present in the new
one when editing quotes "" which
I think no one seems to have
mentioned yet.

As for DUMP,what can I say other
than its name speaks for itself
- it is a load of dump. I can't
believe our good friends Bruce
and Alan first wrote this code
extension then tested it (which
they must have done) and then
thought "Great stuff. This will
do us!".

What RUBBISH!The +3 COPY command
is better and even lets you do a
shaded printout! So now every
time I want to do a graphic dump
I am going to have to load in
FLASH (which prints beautifully
in either DRAFT or FINAL).

By the way, thanks for answering
my question concerning the 255
error and also the SCREEN$ disk
corruption but I can't help
feeling that you are wrong as
even after having formatted the
disk at least three times since
it happened it is stll evident
even with dos 2. Also, as
explained, disk corruption
occurred on my internal drive
when the RESET was pushed but
not on my Lifetime drive when I
had ROM 1. It would now appear

to be the case that BOTH disc
controllers are affected when
RESET is pressed! Luckily, I am
well into the habit of removing
the disks from the drives first.

Tell me out of interest, did you
receive a Dr. Wright's Demo
cassette containing BASIC demos
G.A.U.I. when you were upgraded?
Only U was missing.They enclosed
a disk in the pack so why, oh
why did they not slap all of the
stuff that was on the cassettes
onto that disk as well as just
FLASH, DUMPLD, EMULATOR and the
other odd stuff. Where is the
logic? From now on I will only
believe anything Brucie and Al
tell us when it happens(seeing's
believing as they say).

P.S. The Pink Panther was
excellent.

PPS. A letter in Issue 37 claims
the Star LC10 not to be fully
Epson-compatible . What a load
of rubbish! My LC10C is the same
as the mono LC10 except it is
colour-orientated and my printer
manual says "IBM PROPRINTER II &
EPSON LX800-compatible" so I
think your good reader should
read his manual a bit more
closely.

To Simon Greenfield from Brian

There are two problems I know of
with quotation marks.One is that
if keywords are used they may be
replaced with their character
code while editing (looks like a
splodge). This is not a true bug
but a seemingly necessary side-
effect to using auto-tokenising.
The other problem is a true bug.
If you want a quote in a quote
you must use two quotation marks
as you do on a Spectrum (e.g.,
PRINT "say ""HELLO!"" to Fred")
However, if the string is longer
than 255 bytes then the syntax
checker won't accept the line.
Try replacing the apostrophes in
line 8070 in ALLO ALLO in OUTLET
35 and you'll see!

It should be a straightforward
matter to write a new DUMP and I
have a note in my tray. However,
I estimate about two days work
would be involved and I just
haven't had time... Has anyone
extracted the FLASH dump code
yet and can tell us the address
and length?

The fact that a printer manual
claims to be Epson-compatible
does not mean it is. I've heard
that many printers are slightly
non-compatible even though they
claim to be compatible.

Nothing loads off one side of my
MGT tape so I can't tell about
the demos you mentioned. I'm not
sure it's the same tape anyway.

When a disc is corrupted, part
of the data on the disc is over-
written with new values. This
often means the file will no
longer load at all and the usual
symptom is a track error message
but I suppose it's possible the
corruption may be at the end of
a screen thus ruining the colour
etc. It just seems unlikely that
is the only disc corruption you
get. I mean, are you saying you
save a screen which loads o.k.
then press RESET and thereafter
it is corrupted? I still suspect
that what you describe is NOT
corruption but something else.
Just for interest, try loading
the screen into ANTIFLASH in
Issue 37 to see if it cures the
colours. If so, it's probably
just the FLASH bug.     - Brian

From Steve Monk, ASHFORD
At the last ALL-FORMATS FAIR I
spoke to Mr.Parker of Blue Alpha
Electronics who demonstrated the
latest gizmo for SAM,a voice box
and it works very well. Of even
more interest to me is that
their next project should be a
REALTIME CLOCK.Now we're talking
real computer stuff! Anyway, it
should be launched November
time. Another interesting point
I raised is we can't use these
fancy gadgets all at once due to
the lack of a card cage. Well,
there is news on that subject as
well but I can't confirm when it
will appear because as I left,
Mr. Parker and Alan Miles were
trying to decide who was going
to build it. My money is on Blue
Alpha.

  Edwin Blink, Crouwel str. 60
    9731 M Groningen, HOLLAND

A while ago I got my hands on
some pages from your June issue
of OUTLET. That was the first
time I heard about your tape/
disc magazine. I'm a 19-year-old
Dutch boy. Since February this
year I've been a proud SAM user.
To my knowledge there are three
more SAM users over here in
Holland so you see the SAM has
already gone overseas.

When I got SAM I could not use
the drive as there was no DOS so
I started to examine BASIC and
ROM and, to be sure my soldering
iron didn't get too cold, I made
a printer interface so I could
use my LC10 printer on the SAM.

After this I decided also to
make an EPROM programmer which
came in handy to make a copy of
the ROM 2.0 chip.


A while after that I discovered
that two of the memory chips
(IC's for you techno people)used
in the SAM were less expensive
than 8 64K chips as used in a
Spectrum 128. I could not resist
building a 256K memory extens-
ion. If you're interested in any
of these, just let me know.


I would like to contact other
SAM users so please publish my
full address.

BOOT

- loads DOS if not already in
memory - always from Drive 1 and
loads the AUTO file if on the
disk.


BOOT NUMBER

- loads DOS whether it's already
there or not (so your DVARS will
be changed). This command does
not load the AUTO file.


THE BUG!!

If you've been working with tape
then select DEVICE D and enter
BOOT the DOS tries to load from
tape.

THE REASON!!

If you've been using tape, the
routine for LOAD/SAVE/ VERIFY
copies the device type to the
TEMPORARY device SYSVAR but if
you then enter DEVICE D the
device routine only sets the
PERMANENT device SYSVAR. If you
then enter BOOT everything goes
like normal until the AUTO load
routine jumps back into the load
routine to adjust the pointer
for BASIC. It looks at the
temporary device and since this
is tape it ends up loading from
tape. When you then press the
escape key and enter a BASIC
line the SAM might freeze as the
pointers are incorrect.

THE CURE!!

Simply set the temporary device
after a tape operation to disk
with POKE &5BB7,"D1" OR "D2".

POKES!!!  DPOKE &5AE0,0 to
disable the BREAK button, POKE
&5B41,1 to disable the ESC key.

                  - Edwin Blink


Thanks, Edwin. I've not included
the listings because I couldn't
get 'em to work(typing errors?).
Please send again on disc and I
will put in OUTLET.

Readers should note the SAM ROM
is COPYRIGHT.
                        - Brian

From Malcolm Phillips


Some news for you as regards the
latest ROM for SAM.I went down
to MGT last week to buy the
latest (v3) ROM as Andy Wright
has just completed it. They were
actually blowing the new ROMs in
front of me, and after parting
with the readies I rushed home
and carried out the transplant.

All was well 'till I put in my
Tasword disk and pressed F9. The
DOS boots and then the auto file
loads (I saved Tasword as the
auto file) Great so far. I typed
in a few lines then pressed F9
for the menu.The machine resets!
Another load,F9 - another reset!

I have since found out that it
is not the ROM but the Tasword
BASIC that causes the problem.
Andy Wright has also supplied
the solution, which follows...

After the Tasword BASIC and code
have loaded and you are faced
with the blank(blue)screen ready
for text to be entered, DON'T
press F9 or it will reset SAM.
Press the break button and you
will find yourself in BASIC.
First CLEAR 80000 or you get"out
of memory" when you try to enter
the edited line. Now add to line
1840 the following values:-
Make "&DD" and "&E5" the 4th and
5th DATA values respectively and
make "&DD" and "&E1" the twenty
eighth and twenty ninth values.

All that is left now is to save
the BASIC.

        Yours sincerely,

        Malcolm Phillips

PS I should clarify that Bruce
Gordon and Alan Miles are now
trading as Sam Computers Ltd.


"&" as above is ampersand.

From: W.H.Clarke, WALSALL


Ron & Brian,

Please can you advise me on the
following points...


1) My Plus D only operates on my
Plus 3 Spectrum so can I
transfer items off your disc to
tape to use these items on the
Plus 3, e.g., HIFORM (Issue 35).
Failing this do you know if I
can connect the Plus D Drive
only to the Plus 3 as Drive B?

I am very much a novice yet so
would need simple and detailed
instructions.

2) Do you know of a method of
obtaining composite video
signals from the Plus 3? I use
the 128 for this but would also
like to use the Plus 3 connected
to a video recorder for titling.

           Thank you,

          Bill Clarke.

To Bill Clarke from Brian

I assume there's a misprint in
your letter and you mean your +D
only works on your +2, not +3.
Yes, many OUTLET programs can be
saved from one system and run on
another.Drive options won't work
like BOOT and NEXT ITEM but a +3
program like HIFORM will run on
the +3 correctly. Just use BREAK
and enter SAVE "HIFORM"LINE 9972
to save to tape. Put a disc with
space for the program in your +3
drive ready. When HIFORM loads
from tape it should save to disc
automatically.

A 3.5" drive can be fitted to a
+3 but I don't think you will be
able to load programs saved by
the +D.

A composite video signal can be
obtained by soldering a cable to
the modulator but I'm reluctant
to recommend it to a beginner.

                        - Brian

From Lee Jon Powis, BIRMINGHAM


Does the new DOS read ST disks?
I think if Bo Jangeborg has
bothered to include ST screen
compatibility in FLASH then the
DOS should also be able to read
ST disks -otherwise this feature
is redundant.




No, the new DOS cannot read ST

From Steve Pittman, E. GRINSTEAD

Dear Brian,

Here's a tip for users of LERM's
SAMTAPE.To jazz up your Spectrum
mode a bit -load the 'rom1' file
into 65536,get a font from Flash
or elsewhere and then load that
into 81152. Save "rom1" CODE
65536,16384 and voila - a much
improved Spectrum! Every time
the ROM is loaded, your new font
becomes the Spectrum one.

Now a question or three regard-
ing RAM Paging; q)On page 29 of
the Technical Manual it says
that you can pageout the SYSVARS
etc in block B and replace them
with your own RAM. Now I can get

my head round that OK and can
also see, in that section, how
to temporarily page the SYSVARS
back in via the JSVIN routine to
access ROM routines - BUT what I
don't understand is this :- If I
load LMPR with,for example, page
6 of memory -page 6 will go into
section A and page 7 will go in
section B so I will overwrite
the ROM0 block !!!!! So, how do
I page out section B on its own
when LMPR automatically deals
with A+B together!!

q)I can see how, using JSVIN or
some of the ROM routines,you can
write to the screen indirectly
(the ROM will handle the paging
itself) but assuming I page the
screen into 32768 (where it

should go) how can I write to it
directly when there is only
about 8K left at the top end of
memory and very little available
at the bottom end. Surely they
don't expect you to write code
(including any blocks of data)
into and out of 8K by means of
paging do they !!

I am probably misunderstanding
something somewhere along the
line but that's perhaps because:

a)I am thick.

b)I have only ever messed around
on a 48k Spectrum before and the
last thing you have to mess
about with on one of those is
RAM paging so it's all a bit new
to me!!

Perhaps you could write an
article in OUTLET for dickheads
like me and explain it...


Anyway,I also want to inform you
for the record that I now have
the Version 2 ROM and DOS - and
what a difference!!! I have been
in the process of writing a set
of four simple games (aimed at
the under tens)and up till I got
the new ROM I have spent half
the time trying to write around
ROM bugs and buglets! However,
I've nearly finished them now
and hope to sell them if there
is a market for such things. My
kids and their friends seem to
like them so they can't be that
bad.

I'll let you get on now. Keep up
the GOOD work with SAM - we need
all the support we can get until
things shape up. I read in NCE
this week that SAMs are selling
well since MGT died thanks to
the marketing company. It seems
to me that if MGT had split
itself up into component parts
right at the start maybe they
would have survived a bit better
- but that's the power of hind-
sight I guess...

           Best wishes

          STEVE PITTMAN.

To Steve Pittman from Brian

If you page in say, RAM Pages 6
and 7 to addresses 0 to 32767
then set bit 5 of the LMPR to 0
then the Z80A will access ROM 0
(0 to 16383) and RAM 7 (16384 to
32767). It will not be able to
access RAM 6 although it's paged
in at address 0. If you set bit
5 of the LMPR to 1, however, the
Z80A can then "see" RAM 6.

I've also wondered, like you,how
one should access the screen
with a large code program. I
think the general idea is to put
up to 32K of your code from 0 to
32767 (with perhaps a spare 8K
of data or a workspace at the
top of memory above the screen.

When you want to use the ROM you
reset bit 5 of the LMPR to gain
access (this must be done by the
code above 16383 obviously) and
use JSVIN which will page in the
SYSVARS as needed. If you need
the ROM to operate on some of
your data, say to print some
text, I guess you'd have to copy
it to the top of memory before
calling the ROM.

I would like to hear what other
readers think about this as my
own ideas are very tentative - I
have not actually written any
huge code programs on the SAM -
yet!
                       - Brian

From Mike Jones

Dear Brian,

I note that in your reply to
J.W. Tollett (OUTLETTERS 36) you
advise him that the Tascon+2
conversion is only available to
members of Indug. Well I am a
member of Indug and I sent for a
copy of Tascon+2 and other goods
to the value of `17.45 at the
end of Feb. this year (my cheque
was cashed on the 12th of
March).

Despite repeated 'phone calls to
the editor of Format I still
have not received the goods I
ordered. When I last 'phoned the
Editor in June I asked him to


refund my money. This he refused
to do as he said his liability
had ended when he posted the
goods! He did however promise to
pursue his enquiries as to the
fate of my goods with the Post
Office.

In July I decided it was a waste
of time and money 'phoning the
Editor of Format, so as a last
resort I sent him a letter (by
recorded delivery) asking him to
send me proof of despatch of my
order, or, if he was unable to
do so, to send me the goods or
refund my money within 14 days.
To date (a month later) I have
not even had the courtesy of a
reply. It would appear that I
have been ripped off.

With 'phone calls and postage I
would put the sum of money I
have lost at over `20. Needless
to say I will not be renewing my
membership to Indug if this is
the shoddy way they treat their
members.

So, if anyone knows of an alter-
native Plus D conversion for
Tasword +2 I would grateful if
they would let me know where it
can be obtained.

        Yours Sincerely,

           Mike Jones

To Mike Jones from Brian

Our understanding is that anyone
selling goods by mail order is
responsible for their delivery.
Certainly we operate that way.We
have found the Post Office have
always been willing to pay small
compensation for lost mail- even
non-registered and non-recorded
material. However,I think claims
must come from the sender - not
the receiver. It is a simple
formality which we go through if
any of our own readers do not
receive their order. We just
immediately send a fresh item
and claim from the Post Office.
It may be worth writing to your
local Post Office to inquire if
YOU can claim anyway.

All this still leaves you with
no TASCON+2. Can anyone else
suggest anything or help in any
way or sell Mike an (original)
second-hand TASCON+2?
                        - Brian

From: C.W.G.Coppin, BOSTON.


Dear Messrs. Cavers,

Further to my letter of the 21st
August,I enclose an illustration
of the problem on the new Samdos
Master Disk. I am given to
understand that the program is
not compatible with the Brother
HR Printer which uses an "L"
escape code whereas an Epson
uses a "star" escape code.

You have already produced two
programmes T DEE & G DEE for the
SAM, would they be compatible or
would it be possible to produce
a program to comply with the
Brother HR printer?

There must be quite a lot of HR
printers around and a compatible
dump program would be much
appreciated.

        Yours sincerely,

          C.W.G.Coppin






TEE DEE gives a rapid print-out
of any text (not graphics)on the
screen and should work on ANY
printer. For modifying DUMP,
please read my reply to Julian
Bonnebaigt in OUTLET 37.
                        - Brian.

BOOT

- loads DOS if not already in memory - always from Drive 1 and loads the AUTO file if on the disk.

BOOT NUMBER

THE REASON!!

If you've been using tape, the routine for LOAD/SAVE/ VERIFY copies the device type to the TEMPORARY device SYSVAR but if you then enter DEVICE D the device routine only sets the PERMANENT device SYSVAR. If you page in say, RAM Pages 6 and 7 to addresses 0 to 32767 then set bit 5 of the LMPR to 0 then the Z80A will access ROM 0 (0 to 16383) and RAM 7 (16384 to 32767). When you want to use the ROM you reset bit 5 of the LMPR to gain access (this must be done by the code above 16383 obviously) and use JSVIN which will page in the SYSVARS as needed. Спустя некоторое время я обнаружил, что две микросхемы памяти (IC для вас, технарей), используемые в SAM, стоят дешевле, чем восемь 64K чипов, как в Spectrum 128. Я не смог удержаться и собрал расширение памяти на 256K. Если вас что-то из этого интересует, просто дайте знать.

Я хотел бы связаться с другими пользователями SAM, поэтому, пожалуйста, опубликуйте мой полный адрес.

#### BOOT
Загружает DOS, если она еще не в памяти — всегда с Drive 1, и запускает файл AUTO, если он есть на диске.

#### BOOT NUMBER
Загружает DOS независимо от того, загружена она уже или нет (так что ваши DVARS изменятся). Эта команда не запускает файл AUTO.

#### ОШИБКА!!
Если вы работали с лентой, затем выбрали DEVICE D и ввели BOOT, DOS попытается загрузиться с ленты.

#### ПРИЧИНА!!
Если вы использовали ленту, процедура LOAD/SAVE/VERIFY копирует тип устройства во временную системную переменную (TEMPORARY device SYSVAR), но если вы затем вводите DEVICE D, процедура устройства устанавливает только постоянную системную переменную (PERMANENT device SYSVAR). Если вы затем вводите BOOT, все идет как обычно, пока процедура автозагрузки AUTO не перейдет обратно в процедуру загрузки для корректировки указателя для BASIC. Она смотрит на временное устройство, а так как это лента, все заканчивается попыткой загрузки с кассеты. Если после этого нажать клавишу escape и ввести строку BASIC, SAM может зависнуть, так как указатели некорректны.

#### ЛЕЧЕНИЕ!!
Просто установите временное устройство после работы с лентой на диск с помощью:
`POKE &5BB7,"D1"` ИЛИ `"D2"`.

ПОКИ!!!  
`DPOKE &5AE0,0` — отключить кнопку BREAK,  
`POKE &5B41,1` — отключить клавишу ESC.

— Edwin Blink
